clue.text: Imp deviously tucked into food for squirrel

indicators.note: the reworked letters are tucked inside the word for food, like a filling

parts.note: chuck is slang for food, as in chuck wagon

indicators.note: acting deviously means going by a crooked route, so the letters of imp are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mischievous sprite sneaks something into a squirrel's dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'food for squirrel' reads as one phrase, but food is the outer piece and squirrel alone is the definition. Chipmuck is an old variant spelling of chipmunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipmuck is a small striped ground squirrel of North America, the chipmunk under an older spelling.

clue.text: Eggs laid in alternative to hay stuff

definitions.note: stuff in the sense of nonsense, as in stuff and nonsense

indicators.note: eggs are laid, and here they are laid inside the other word

parts.note: hey is an alternative spelling of hay, the old country dance
two O shapes, eggs being oval

explanation.surface: A farmyard picture of hens laying among straw-like fodder.
explanation.walkthrough: Hay here is the dance (also spelt hey), not dried grass, despite the eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooey is slang for nonsense, and stuff, as an exclamation, dismisses talk as nonsense.

clue.text: Relatives of woodpecker, one cat topped

definitions.note: plural, because Iynx names the whole genus of wrynecks

indicators.note: a topped word has lost its top, its first letter, in a down entry

parts.note: the lynx is a wild cat

explanation.surface: Birds related to the woodpecker, with a cat that has been killed off.
explanation.walkthrough: Topped is a slang word for killed, which fits a cat among birds, but here it means the first letter is lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Iynx is the wryneck genus, birds of the woodpecker family, so the name covers a group of the woodpecker's kin.

clue.text: Petit-bourgeois passion to climb in what's 'smart'

indicators.note: the climbing pair sits inside the word for smart

parts.note: posh, smart and upper-class

indicators.note: in a down answer, climbing means the words passion and to are read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: ire is anger, a passion
taken as written: the little word itself climbs along with the passion

explanation.surface: Small-minded social climbing in pursuit of what counts as smart.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is from Mr Pooter, the self-important clerk of the Grossmiths' The Diary of a Nobody. Note that 'to' is part of what climbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooterish describes the genteel, self-important narrowness of the lower middle class, like Charles Pooter in the comic novel.

clue.text: Traditional game — league retained by clubs

definitions.note: merels, the old board game also called nine men's morris

indicators.note: the letter for league is held inside the clubs

parts.note: a mere is a Maori war club, so meres are clubs

explanation.surface: An old sport kept going within a league by its member clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: The clubs are weapons, not sporting clubs: a mere is a Maori war club of greenstone.
explanation.definitionFit: Merels, or nine men's morris, is an ancient board game of placing and moving counters on a grid.

clue.text: One responsible for pitch, we hear, in period of play

indicators.note: what we hear is the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: a chucker is one who chucks, that is pitches or throws

explanation.surface: Talk of a groundsman or bowler and a spell of play in some sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Pitch suggests the field; it means throw. In a non-rhotic accent chucker and chukka sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A chukka is one of the timed periods into which a polo match is divided.

clue.text: Fate placing the writer in coffin

indicators.note: the writer is placed inside the coffin
marks the writer going inside the coffin

parts.note: kist is a Scots word for a chest or coffin
the setter referring to himself, so me

explanation.surface: A gloomy author imagines destiny putting him into his coffin.
explanation.definitionFit: Kismet is destiny or fate, from a Turkish word meaning one's portion or lot.

clue.text: Country gardener

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the West African state

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a rustic gardener; the two words are separate meanings of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked republic in West Africa, and in Indian English the same word names a gardener.

clue.text: Horse, adult, frenzied, I had docked

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so the end of the word is removed

parts.note: rabid, wildly frantic
contracted to I'd

explanation.surface: A grown horse runs wild and its tail is cut.
explanation.walkthrough: Docked fits horses, whose tails are docked, but here it cuts I'D from the end of another word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arab is a breed of horse famed for speed and stamina, from the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: I lost trick being trapped by girl, unruly

indicators.note: the shortened trick is caught inside the word for girl

parts.note: a lass

indicators.note: the letter I goes missing from the trick

parts.note: a wile is a cunning trick

explanation.surface: Someone loses a trick at cards and is caught out by a wild girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawless means not governed by law, hence disorderly and unruly.

clue.text: Link involved with Parisian ground, behindhand

parts.note: in, as in being in on something
terre is French for earth or ground
late, behind time

explanation.surface: Something about a link with French soil and lateness.
explanation.walkthrough: Parisian points to French, as it usually does in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To interrelate is to connect or bring into a mutual relationship, so it can stand for link as a verb.

clue.text: Germanic of a kind? Varied roots run deep, mostly

indicators.note: varied means changed, so the letters of roots are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
go, as in run or go to a place

indicators.note: most of the word, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: thick, as in a deep or thick layer

explanation.surface: Germanic peoples' varied origins run deep.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals that this is one particular Germanic tongue or people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ostrogoths were the eastern Goths, a Germanic people, so Ostrogothic names one kind of Germanic.

clue.text: Like a marine invertebrate, form of headless sea-urchin

indicators.note: a new form of the letters, so they are rearranged
the word loses its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something resembling a sea creature, shaped like a sea urchin without a head.
explanation.definitionFit: Echiuran is the adjective for the Echiura, spoon worms living in marine burrows.

clue.text: Full-voiced native to get excited endlessly about nothing

indicators.note: the pieces go around the letter for nothing

parts.note: a son of a place is one born there

indicators.note: a word used endlessly has no end, so the final letter of the excited word is cut off

parts.note: rouse, to stir up or excite
O, the round zero

explanation.surface: A local gets worked up over nothing at all and becomes loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonorous describes a deep, resonant voice or sound, so it fits a booming, full-voiced speaker.

clue.text: Scottish mat, wide, incorporated in E. Indian matting

definitions.note: a verb here: tawt is Scots for to mat or tangle

indicators.note: the letter for wide goes inside the matting

parts.note: tat is coarse East Indian fabric used as matting

explanation.surface: A Scottish rug and a broad piece of Indian matting.
explanation.walkthrough: Mat looks like a noun beside matting; it is a verb, to tangle into a mass.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots, to tawt hair or wool is to tangle it into a matted knot.

clue.text: One sending message in part broadcast externally

indicators.note: only part of the two words is used, the answer sitting across their join

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A person sending a message as part of a broadcast to the outside world.
explanation.walkthrough: Broadcast and externally both look like instructions, but they are simply the words that hold the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A texter is someone who sends text messages from a mobile phone.

clue.text: Met ship foundering south of Asian capital, the work of brigands

indicators.note: in a down entry, south means below, so the anagram comes after

parts.note: Kuala Lumpur, capital of Malaysia, by its initials

indicators.note: a foundering ship breaks up, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A meeting with a ship sinking off the coast below a Malaysian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Klephts were Greek bandits who held out in the mountains against Ottoman rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Klephtism is brigandage, the way of life of the Greek klephts, outlaw bands of the mountains.

clue.text: Short lines, not many lacking width, prevalent in old poetry

parts.note: RY, short for railway, the lines

indicators.note: the letter for width is missing

parts.note: few

explanation.surface: Brief verses that, without breadth, are common in early poems.
explanation.walkthrough: Lines is a railway, abbreviated RY, not lines of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ryfe is an old spelling of rife, meaning widespread or prevalent, found in early poets like Spenser.

clue.text: Beetle to cause alarm in places? Lot losing heart kept inside

definitions.note: a verb here, fair because beetle is used in Britain for scurrying about, as in beetle off down the road

indicators.note: the shortened lot is held inside the other word

parts.note: skeer is a dialect form of scare, used in some regions

indicators.note: a word losing its heart loses its centre, so the middle letter of lot drops out

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A beetle spreading alarm in certain places.
explanation.walkthrough: Beetle looks like the insect; it is the verb, to scurry about. In places marks a regional word.
explanation.definitionFit: To skelter is to scurry or rush along, as in helter-skelter, matching beetle meaning to hurry.

clue.text: Exaggerates distance abroad covered by polar hero

indicators.note: the distance is wrapped by the explorer's name

parts.note: Captain Oates of Scott's Antarctic expedition
a verst is an old Russian measure of distance

explanation.surface: Someone inflating how far a famous explorer travelled overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: Lawrence Oates walked out to his death on Scott's return from the South Pole.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstate is to claim more than is true, so it equals exaggerate.

clue.text: Window in nave, cracked, letting sun in

indicators.note: the cracked letters let the word for sun come inside
marks the sun going inside
broken, so the letters of nave are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
tan, as in to sun oneself

explanation.surface: A church window, broken, lets sunlight into the nave.
explanation.definitionFit: Ventana is the Spanish word for a window, used in English in the American Southwest.

clue.text: Club poem's recast, causing ßuster

definitions.note: the clue's fl ligature rendered as one character: fluster, a verb

parts.note: a disco, a nightclub

indicators.note: recast means cast again in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Rewriting a club's poem leaves someone flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is fluster, printed with a damaged fl ligature.
explanation.definitionFit: To discompose is to disturb someone's composure, which is to agitate or fluster them.

clue.text: Regarding early Irish immigrants, I brought in block (not the last)

indicators.note: the letter I is put inside
the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to scotch a wheel is to block it with a wedge
taken as written

explanation.surface: Settlers from Ireland once blocked from entry.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scoti were Irish settlers in western Scotland, who gave the country its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotic relates to the ancient Scots, Irish Gaels who settled in Argyll from about the fifth century.

clue.text: No. 2 in pub opening quantity of bottles? Possibly

definitions.text: No. 2 in pub opening quantity of bottles? Possibly

indicators.note: the letter opens up the crate by going inside it

parts.note: a crate holds a quantity of bottles

indicators.note: the second letter of the word pub

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A deputy at the pub opens a crate of bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue pictures an assistant at work; a curate is the vicar's No. 2, the question mark softening the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate is a parish priest's assistant, his second-in-command, here jokingly put in charge at a pub.

clue.text: Obscure insect found in climbing tree

indicators.note: the insect is found inside the climbing tree, as a bug might be found in its bark
going up a down entry, so the tree is reversed

parts.note: elm
ant

explanation.surface: An unidentified bug spotted on a tree it is climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: Obscure looks like an adjective about the insect; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To mantle is to cloak or cover, so it means to obscure from view.

clue.text: Woodlice disconcerted cousins

definitions.note: plural, as Oniscus is the genus of common woodlice

indicators.note: thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Relatives upset by woodlice in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Oniscus is the genus of the common woodlouse, so the name stands for these crustaceans.

clue.text: Head (see) disposed of rustic cat

definitions.note: a verb here, fair because cat is old British slang for to vomit, just as hurl is

explanation.walkthrough: Cat is slang for to be sick, so it is a verb, not an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurl is slang for vomit, and cat has the same meaning in old British slang.

clue.text: Advanced in rank from nothing at Mons around end thereof

indicators.note: the French nothing goes round the letter

indicators.note: the last letter of the town just named

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: Mug drunk with a dash of water in

indicators.note: the clue ends with in, telling us the dash of water is put in the drunk

parts.note: a sot

indicators.note: only a little, the first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: Mug looks like a cup; it is to study hard.

clue.text: Small constellation? There's lines solemn Scot composed with this one

definitions.text: Small constellation? There's lines solemn Scot composed with this one

indicators.note: composed means put together, so these letters plus the answer are arranged into the opening phrase

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, so lines gives two of them

clue.text: Light now rarely seen in the battlements

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: Idle women getting stuck into hock

clue.text: Part of Burns night menu, tons of minimum quality

clue.text: Fatty substance, one in blended lotions

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: One famous for severity? Requires working on in company

clue.text: About to be buried in mortar — equivalent of this for ill-fated gangster?

re, meaning concerning
